new_valid_findings.reason: Each unnamed socket accumulates active-room broadcasts with no cap/deadline. Runtime needed for exhaustion threshold; frequent activity prevents idle memory reset.

new_valid_findings.title: Cooldown timer prevents hibernation
new_valid_findings.reason: Room-side limiter waits via timer; large shared-IP cooldowns can keep idle rooms resident. Actual bill remains deployment-dependent.

new_valid_findings.title: Invalid route/Upgrade reaches DO
new_valid_findings.reason: Valid-shaped room IDs are resolved/dispatched before invalid suffix or missing Upgrade is rejected. Front-Worker validation avoids needless DO calls; malformed namespace IDs can fail earlier.

new_valid_findings.title: Uninstall historical migration mismatch
new_valid_findings.reason: README new_classes differs from frozen new_sqlite_classes. Preserve actual applied historical definition; no claim of proven actual uninstall failure is needed.

new_valid_findings.title: Missing explicit close reply at configured old date
new_valid_findings.reason: Close handler lacks close() and configured 2024 date predates 2026-04-07 automatic replies. Explicit close is a sound targeted fix; deployed compatibility overrides remain unknown.

new_valid_findings.title: Fresh local limiter admits introduction before remote reply
new_valid_findings.reason: First valid frame on a fresh socket is admitted before the shared response, allowing many concurrent introductions/join broadcasts. It does not itself reach subsequent chat-history storage; claims about stored-chat bypass need a complete post-introduction sequence.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Broadcast before initiating persistence
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Source broadcast precedes put; report considers output-gate ordering, so existing gates do not automatically refute it. Actual peer visibility if the later put fails requires runtime fault injection. README:11 deliberately describes live relay directly and storage only for history, so stronger atomic live/history semantics need a contract. High confidence should refer to ordering, not observed loss.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: No persisted history cleanup
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: No cleanup exists but no exactly100 retention promise exists either. Report largely keeps storage severity as evidence request.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Possible submit-button double startChat
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Native button/form default actions and element removal during click handler matter; report explicitly requests browser testing and does not claim reproduction.

other_accuracy_notes.quote: parallel sockets from one IP can each admit an initial message before the shared limiter replies
other_accuracy_notes.correction: True for introduction/join events; initial user-info branch returns before storage.put. Test should explicitly distinguish introduction acceptance from subsequent chat persistence rather than assume simultaneous first frames write history.

other_accuracy_notes.quote: reconnect is fixed at ten seconds without jitter
other_accuracy_notes.correction: The code enforces ten seconds since connection start only for short-lived connections; a socket open longer than ten seconds reconnects immediately on close. More precise is 'minimum ten-second start-to-start interval for rapid failures, no jitter'. This is a minor precision issue, not a different retry mechanism.

other_accuracy_notes: Moving the name into the upgrade changes the handshake protocol as the report acknowledges. It is an optional valid redesign; a bounded first-frame protocol can also fix buffering while preserving the client contract.
Persisting blockedUntil in an attachment is a real hibernation-aware limiter-control improvement, although it does not diagnose C1's independently lost pending history.
Accepted-message cost proxy is best read as accepted chat messages; first user-info frames do not write history and locally rejected cooldown frames do not call the limiter.
reviews.control_handling: Correctly credits bounded list reads, async KV on SQLite, real Hibernation API and configured migrations. Close-date finding is tied to a concrete protocol semantic; no broad get/put race claim.
reviews.overall: Useful timer/buffer/front-boundary/close findings, C1 missed. Broadcast-before-write is conditional and contract-sensitive, not a categorical storage-gate falsehood. Some limiter and reconnect wording needs protocol/timing precision.

primary_mechanisms.reason: Concurrent same-ID read/check/write allows duplicate enqueues; proposes authoritative per-event DO state.
Send failure after KV status causes retry early-return without enqueue repair; explicit pending/enqueued recovery fixes the actual cross-store boundary.
Explains final ack after stale/missing KV event read and recommends authoritative DO read or bounded queue envelope.
Explicit already-half-open allowance lets multiple reservations through before first result. Identifies exact pure-policy mechanism without unsupported lost-update claim.

new_valid_findings.title: Status returns attempts belonging to other same-destination events
new_valid_findings.reason: Per-destination DO table and query lack event_id despite event-specific route. Explicitly makes multi-user disclosure conditional and recommends ownership only if multi-tenant.

new_valid_findings.title: Raw URL spellings split destination-control identity
new_valid_findings.reason: DO identity uses unnormalized caller URL while fetch interprets URLs. Equivalent spellings such as host casing or an explicit default HTTPS port can target one endpoint through separate token buckets/circuits. Requires an intended canonical endpoint identity and operational demonstration for exact abuse magnitude; it is not evidence of private-network SSRF.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: External side-effect/ack ambiguity
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Stable webhook-id exists; repeated queue processing or crash after remote commit can repeat effects unless receiver dedupes. Correctly says local delivered check cannot close the external uncertainty window. README promises idempotent ingest, not exactly-once receiver effects.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Gate denials consume retry budget and attempt counter
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: retry counts gate deferrals toward max_retries and can route an event to DLQ with fewer/no HTTP attempts. Status attempts takes queue delivery count; it is not an explicit outbound-call counter. Separate outbound and gate counts is good observability but the need for a separate scheduler/deadline is an SLO choice.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Public relay exposure
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Report explicitly conditions high severity on public routing and acknowledges README auth omission. Auth, quotas and destination policy are deployment hardening for this focused reference, not proof of an undisclosed hosted-service boundary violation.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Permanent 4xx affects destination health
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Consumer reports success only for delivered outcomes, so permanent HTTP failures increment circuit failure count. Whether e.g. invalid credentials indicates unhealthy destination is a product/policy choice; no source promise limits health state to transient failures. Report partly acknowledges this with 'unless ... intentionally part of that policy'.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Attempt-table lookup/retention cost
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Schema has no ordering index and no retention. Report correctly leaves exact rows examined/billing unknown. Retention must be defined before cleanup.

significant_wrong_fixes_or_tests.quote: add tests proving permanent outcomes do not open the circuit.
significant_wrong_fixes_or_tests.correction: First define the destination-health policy. Treating repeated permanent endpoint/auth/configuration failures as health failures can be intentional and is what the current code consistently does. A test banning it is not a required correctness invariant; the single-half-open-probe test is independently valid.

other_accuracy_notes: Rejects no-DLQ, missing-backoff and dead-RPC leads after source review; good control handling.

H4 fix should include a lease expiry/recovery path, not merely permanently deny half-open state after an abandoned probe. The report's broader per-event recovery state does not explicitly solve per-destination abandoned probe recovery.
The comment about gate deferrals refers to avoiding an attempt's worth of effort; retry accounting remains true independently of whether the comment promises a distinct logical budget.
reviews.control_handling: Credits actual queue/DLQ dispatch, finite retry/backoff, receiver webhook-id, DO authority and private per-object storage. Does not claim DO get/put races or missing terminal handler.
reviews.overall: All H1–H4 detected with concrete recovery-oriented fixes. Additional event-history/canonicalization risks are useful. Public exposure, receiver dedupe, gate budgets and permanent-4xx health policy are conditional; one proposed test imposes an unestablished policy.

primary_mechanisms.reason: Concurrent negative KV reads allow duplicate enqueue; per-event DO claim/status recommended.
Persisted status before send leaves orphaned queued state and blocks same-ID repair; recommends explicit recovery scheduling.
No diagnosis of consumer final-ack on temporarily missing event envelope. General stale authoritative state discussion is focused on ingress/status, not null-envelope loss.
Already-half-open state permits later probes; proposes lease and crash expiry. Correctly does not infer storage input-gate lost-update races.

new_valid_findings.title: Duplicate consumers can regress terminal status
new_valid_findings.reason: Status writes are unconditional; duplicate consumers with differing outcomes may overwrite terminal state. Per-event monotonic coordination is sound.

new_valid_findings.title: Sustained terminal-consumer status-write failure can exhaust retries
new_valid_findings.reason: The configured DLQ has an active consumer with default finite retries and no further configured dead-letter target. If setStatus repeatedly fails through that retry budget, its queue message can be discarded before terminal status/logging completes. This is conditional sustained dependency failure, not a missing primary DLQ. Original event envelope remains in KV, so total payload erasure is not established. README's 'recorded and logged, never dropped' is stronger than this bounded terminal-recording path guarantees.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: At-least-once external webhook side effects
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Stable webhook-id is present and acknowledged. A per-event claim reduces concurrent/replayed work but cannot atomically commit an external HTTP effect with local queue acknowledgement; receiver dedupe is the actual stronger-contract requirement. No exactly-once effect promise is shown.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Gate retries can dead-letter without outbound work
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Gate denials consume max_retries. Separate bounded scheduler may meet a stronger delivery SLO; it is not mandatory merely because retries are finite.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: No ordering index/retention on destination attempts
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Schema lacks at index and rows append forever. Report appropriately asks query plan/usage and retention requirements. An index helps ORDER BY LIMIT20; bounded retention is still a chosen policy.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Before-public-deployment auth/URL/size controls
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Recommendations are explicitly before public deployment and private-target reachability remains an evidence question. README intentionally excludes hosted multi-tenant auth.

other_accuracy_notes.correction: The existing terminal handler already awaits setStatus before logging and ack. A separate independent replay/quarantine store could address exhausted terminal retries, but simply reordering persistence before ack is redundant. A single injected write failure currently retries correctly; test sustained failures through the configured/default terminal retry limit to expose the actual new risk.

other_accuracy_notes.quote: every DLQ event must have exhausted actual HTTP attempts
other_accuracy_notes.correction: This is a proposed stronger policy, not a universal correctness rule. Separate age/deadline/admission exhaustion can legitimately be terminal if explicitly chosen and accurately reported. Test the agreed budget/termination contract rather than forcing all DLQ reasons to be outbound-failure counts.

other_accuracy_notes: Adding another DLQ layer alone cannot guarantee infinite preservation under arbitrary prolonged failure; durable independent quarantine/reconciliation and explicit retention/alerting assumptions are needed.

The report misses mixed-event attempt attribution: its index/retention finding is destination-wide and does not propose event_id filtering. This is a new valid non-oracle opportunity, not another H1–H4 miss.
reviews.control_handling: Acknowledges and inspects the existing terminal DLQ consumer rather than asserting no DLQ. Correctly credits await-before-ack behavior insofar as source ordering is shown; terminal persistence recommendation is partly redundant and needs exhaustion-specific verification. No unsupported DO storage race.
reviews.overall: H1/H2/H4 detected, H3 missed. Sustained DLQ-consumer dependency-failure exhaustion is a valid conditional new terminal-recording risk, with envelope-survival and existing persist-before-ack controls explicitly preserved. Gate budgeting and receiver effects remain contract/SLO matters.

new_valid_findings.reason: Attempt schema/query lacks event_id and event-specific status endpoint returns destination-wide rows. Public multi-caller disclosure is conditional and acknowledged. Event filtering/schema migration/index are appropriate.

new_valid_findings.title: Terminal consumer retries can exhaust during sustained status-write failure
new_valid_findings.reason: Main queue does have DLQ, but its active consumer has finite default retries and no further sink. Repeated setStatus failure through that budget can discard queue notification before terminal state is recorded. Event envelope persists in KV, so full payload erasure is not shown. Report correctly retains existing process-before-ack ordering and tests failure beyond retry limit.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: External effect/ack ambiguity
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Acknowledges stable webhook-id and correctly recommends recipient dedupe for at-least-once processing. README's idempotent-ingest promise does not guarantee exactly-once external effects.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Public relay/auth/quotas
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Report conditions abuse/disclosure on public deployment, but auth/tenant/destination authorization is intentionally outside focused reference scope. Source exposure is true; mandatory auth closure presumes a deployment trust contract.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Permanent outcomes increment circuit health failures
conditional_or_policy_findings.quote: circuit breaker violates both failure and half-open policy
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Half-open violates an explicit single-probe promise. No independent source policy says permanent 4xx must never influence destination health; individual retry classification and health aggregation can legitimately differ. The source scenario of invalid requests delaying later valid requests is real, but whether unacceptable is a policy decision.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Attempt retention/query work
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: No ordering index or cleanup exists. Report accurately asks query plan/metrics rather than assuming LIMIT20 bounds rows examined. Destructive retention still requires defined policy.

Permanent means do not retry that same event; repeated endpoint/auth/configuration errors may legitimately affect destination health. Define which outcome/status classes affect circuit health before making this a universal test. Tests should assert that chosen policy, not impose it from retry classification alone.

other_accuracy_notes: Immediate retry on missing KV event is a valid interim mitigation, not complete recovery beyond arbitrary KV visibility delay; stronger authoritative-store/outbox design is explicitly provided.

Adding a further terminal queue only moves the final-retention boundary; durable replay store/reconciliation, retry/retention assumptions and monitoring are necessary for a quantified never-drop contract.
Does not explicitly discuss gate deferrals consuming the delivery retry budget; that is an SLO-dependent non-primary issue rather than an H1–H4 miss.
reviews.control_handling: Explicitly credits the primary configured DLQ and live DO RPC methods; terminal retry-exhaustion finding targets actual active terminal consumer. Does not claim a missing primary DLQ or unprotected storage get/put race.
reviews.overall: All H1–H4 detected. Additional per-event history and conditional terminal-recording loss are valid. Permanent-4xx health rule/test is an unestablished policy; public auth and exactly-once receiver effects need contract scope.

new_valid_findings.reason: No event_id is stored or filtered. Properly asks old-row migration/backfill behavior. Disclosure to another tenant needs a multi-user deployment boundary not defined by this reference.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Repeated queue deliveries can repeat remote side effects
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Report clearly recognizes receiver runtime contract is unknown and local state cannot guarantee exactly-once effects. Stable webhook-id is credited. This is a valid operational contract question, not proof the source promised exactly-once.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Finite retries also count local gate denial
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Repeated denial can exhaust retries before actual HTTP attempts. Proposed bounded deferral counter and intentional deferral-limit failure is appropriately explicit about a chosen policy rather than requiring unlimited wait.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Permanent outcomes affect destination circuit
conditional_or_policy_findings.quote: the circuit breaker neither single-probes nor respects outcome class
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: One probe is explicitly promised. Different per-event retry classes need not map one-to-one to circuit health classes; repeated payload-specific 400s can block later events but desired treatment depends on policy. Report partially recognizes explicit 410/429 policy is required.

conditional_or_policy_findings.title: Auth omission before public ingress
conditional_or_policy_findings.reason: Report explicitly recognizes README deliberate auth exclusion and asks whether publicly exposed; no mandatory hosted-product auth defect is asserted.

CREATE TABLE defines no at index and rows append without cleanup. LIMIT does not establish constant rows examined or constant SQL work. A query plan/runtime metrics should determine exact work instead of declaring the path bounded; the report itself later calls the table unbounded.

A receiver claim/terminal check reduces concurrent/replayed work while receiver dedupe closes external-effect uncertainty; the report correctly states local exact-once is impossible.

primary_mechanisms.evidence_quote: use nonexistent binding `PB` and operate only on KV although paste identity now resides in D1.
primary_mechanisms.assessment: Correctly identifies both obsolete binding and failure to act on authoritative D1 rows; proposed D1-aware listing/deletion addresses mechanism.

secondary_mechanisms.evidence_quote: two requests for the same custom name can both observe absence and the later write silently replaces the first paste and its admin password.
secondary_mechanisms.assessment: Correct source interleaving, with conditional can rather than a claim of reproduced exploitation. Separate plain INSERT for create and conditional update are sensible.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: Severity: high — D1/KV lifecycle is incomplete
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: KV retention is source-real but README.md:31 expressly documents retaining expired big payloads to save writes; db.js:162-165 deliberately deletes the authoritative row. This is an accepted storage-lifecycle tradeoff to disclose/optionally improve, not by itself a high undisclosed leak. Report does acknowledge README but still elevates it into a leading release defect. No confidential content becomes publicly reachable through D1 after its row is deleted.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: Severity: high — default uploads are unbounded by source admission controls
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: Anonymous default uploading is a documented public pastebin capability; BASIC_AUTH is explicitly optional. No evidence requires closed production access. Lack of application rate/streaming bounds is a separate defensible hardening/cost concern whose deployed materiality is unknown; do not label the intended open mode an authentication defect.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: clean environments cannot derive schema through the deployment workflow, rerunning bootstrap destroys data
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: The deploy workflow does not initialize schema, but README.md:41 explicitly directs the operator to create D1 and apply schema manually and warns that doing so resets all data. A clean deployment following that prerequisite can have the table. Automated non-destructive migrations are an improvement; there is no source proof of a silently destructive automatic upgrade. Missing local/test schema setup remains a conditional concern needing pinned runtime evidence.

wrong_proposed_fixes_or_tests.quote: make production upload admission fail closed before reading the body
wrong_proposed_fixes_or_tests.assessment: Makes documented default public uploading fail unless a new private-production requirement is adopted. Preserve optional BASIC_AUTH or make the product-policy change explicit.

wrong_proposed_fixes_or_tests.quote: unauthenticated and oversized requests must cause zero D1/KV operations
wrong_proposed_fixes_or_tests.assessment: Zero storage work for unauthenticated uploads is correct only when BASIC_AUTH is configured and nonempty. As an unconditional default test it rejects intended public mode. Oversize limit validation before storage is sensible.

Any added TTL must preserve no-expiry pastes, renewed expiry on updates, and references to versioned payloads. Generic TTL addition cannot be assumed to fix cross-store lifecycle safely. Report's versioned-key and reconciliation proposals are otherwise appropriate.

additional_valid_findings.assessment: Source-valid: common.js escapeHtml substitutes only &,<,> despite quote map; pages/highlight.js inserts lang in a single-quoted class. A quote-bearing lang can add an event attribute. This is an additional valid security mechanism, but src/pages/* presentation review was explicitly out of the frozen audit scope; record separately rather than using it to inflate in-scope recall.

Correctly observes non-cryptographic randomness for generated administration passwords. Replacing it with crypto randomness is appropriate; source alone does not demonstrate feasible prediction or compromise.

additional_valid_findings.mechanism: Expired default read returns a placeholder 200
additional_valid_findings.assessment: Default raw GET reaches new Response(item.value) with the non-null expiredItemTemplate.value string. Returning null after deleting expired row would match ordinary not-found behavior. No actual expiry test was run; role-specific markdown/highlight/redirect branches may differ because decode expects byte input.
KV get null becomes empty Uint8Array, and PUT across KV/D1 has no atomic commit. Valid conditional robustness concerns; exact global staleness, incident rate, or monetary loss remain unmeasured.

additional_valid_findings.mechanism: Buffers multipart body before enforcing content size
additional_valid_findings.assessment: Correctly identifies await request.arrayBuffer before checking parsed content.length against MAX_LEN. Platform limits and deployment controls constrain actual abuse; a source application limit/streaming design is reasonable without changing public authorization intent.

storage-config.auth_guard_assessment: Preserves PUT/DELETE capability-password intent and correctly recognizes nodejs_compat/test-only Node use. Does not invent SQL injection. The public-upload hardening section improperly turns optional authentication into a required policy.
storage-config.expiry_cache_assessment: Correct about source KV retention and default placeholder status; no cache-expiry execution evidence. No claim that retained orphan bytes remain accessible through deleted D1 rows should be inferred.
storage-config.overall: Primary defect found, secondary race found, several useful additional source findings. Main weaknesses are severity/policy inflation around explicitly public uploads, documented retention, and manual bootstrap.
storage-config.review_method: Read only opaque report, original frozen source/oracle, and primary docs. No skill/scanner source, arm map, judge scores, target execution, or deployed requests.

primary_mechanisms.evidence_quote: Any valid uploader—or a broken client—can place arbitrary bytes under another object’s SHA-256 OID and overwrite it.
primary_mechanisms.assessment: Correct authenticated threat model and hash/key mismatch; does not claim auth bypass or that Git LFS silently trusts mismatching data.

secondary_mechanisms.evidence_quote: Existing objects should omit upload actions, not report an error.
secondary_mechanisms.assessment: Correct Git LFS deduplication mechanism and existing-object 409 location.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: Severity: high — Revocation is not immediately authoritative
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: Eventual KV revocation is a valid platform limitation, but README.md:40-41 does not promise instantaneous global revocation. The report's conditional remedies are sound; high severity as a release defect requires an immediacy requirement not established by this project.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: A fresh deployment cannot establish binding IDs, compatibility date, routes, public R2 hostname, or the precise KV schema from the repository.
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: The repository intentionally uses manual binding setup; README.md:15-21 names required bindings and secret generation, and :42-43 directs URL constant customization. Not shipping resource IDs or Wrangler does not establish misdeployment. There is a useful documentation ambiguity: tokenId must be the KV key with a truthy value, while README loosely says add token. Exact public-domain creation could also be documented better. Distinguish that gap from a blanket unreproducibility defect.

repair_assessment.quote: Canonicalize the OID to lowercase and pass its decoded value as R2’s `sha256` `put` option
repair_assessment.assessment: Correct option/mechanism; raw digest ArrayBuffer or accepted hex string is appropriate, not an S3-only checksum header. Matching body hashes prevent arbitrary-byte overwrite; idempotent retry advice is sensible. Explicit atomic onlyIf handling could strengthen immutable-create behavior but is not mandatory to fix checksum mismatch.

repair_assessment.quote: Tie the batch-declared size to a short-lived upload grant
repair_assessment.assessment: Possible stricter protocol design; increases state/policy beyond minimal fix. No demonstrated existing size-bound requirement is bypassed. Not marked a wrong fix.

repair_assessment.quote: omit actions for already-present uploads
repair_assessment.assessment: Correct; must omit the error too, as report context indicates.

additional_valid_findings.assessment: Valid source work-amplification concern: each valid OID incurs a head and no application byte/object cap exists. Report says application-unbounded and avoids exact billing. Physical request/platform limits still bound executions; no measured abuse incident is established.

additional_valid_findings.mechanism: Batch auth/malformed errors wrapped in HTTP 200
additional_valid_findings.assessment: Valid protocol defect. handleRequest wraps returned JSON string in 200; auth failure prevents KV/R2 write but fails status-driven credential discovery. Returning 4xx and LFS-Authenticate where appropriate is useful.
Valid qualified concern, not an auth bypass; report correctly allows documenting accepted latency instead of requiring strong consistency.
Useful additional documentation gap: code keys by payload.tokenId; README's add token language is imprecise. Lack of explicit resource IDs is not itself a defect.

storage-config.auth_guard_assessment: No false /generate bypass, public-download exposure, self-revoke bypass, arbitrary object ownership policy, missing waitUntil, or source-secret claim. Signature plus KV authorization is preserved.
storage-config.expiry_cache_assessment: Correctly treats exact revocation window and external cache configuration as unmeasured; severity overstates an undocumented instantaneous-revocation policy.
storage-config.overall: Both oracle mechanisms found with actionable correct checksum/protocol repairs. Additional fanout and error-status findings valid. Manual-deployment and revocation severity claims need qualification.
storage-config.review_method: Read only opaque report, original frozen source/oracle, and primary docs. No skill/scanner source, arm map, judge scores, target execution, or deployed requests.

primary_mechanisms.evidence_quote: A token holder can store arbitrary bytes under another object’s SHA-256 name or replace a valid object
primary_mechanisms.assessment: Correct authenticated integrity concern and exact direct PUT path, without inventing upload authorization bypass.

secondary_mechanisms.assessment: Correctly identifies existing-object idempotency defect and proposes omitting actions instead of treating existing content as an error.

material_false_claims.quote: `project/` contains no Wrangler configuration or deployment procedure.
material_false_claims.correction: No Wrangler exists, but saying no procedure elides README.md:15-21 binding names/secret generation and :29-43 manual KV/token workflow and constant customization, plus local client setup thereafter. These are incomplete manual instructions, not no instructions. No source proof shows the manually configured bindings are absent.
material_false_claims.materiality: Partially false compound premise drives a medium misconfiguration finding. The narrower tokenId/schema and public-domain documentation gaps remain valid.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: A revoked, indefinitely valid token may therefore continue uploading temporarily.
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: May is correctly qualified and KV lag is real. Generated tokens deliberately have no exp and remain authorized only while their tokenId is truthy in KV. Absence of exp/issuer/audience enforcement is a hardening/policy question, not a source-proven cross-app authorization defect without shared-key or temporal requirements.

overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.quote: The documented manual deployment is not reproducible
overstatements_or_control_misclassificat.correction: Manual environment setup is the intended deployment model. Lack of Wrangler, compatibility date, resource IDs, or route exports is not evidence that actual deployment fails. Better tokenId mapping and public-domain instructions are useful; missing account artifacts should remain an environment hypothesis.

repair_assessment.quote: Pass the OID as R2’s `sha256` integrity option and use `onlyIf: If-None-Match: *`
repair_assessment.assessment: Mechanism is correct. This is schematic syntax; an actual implementation must pass a Headers object for If-None-Match (or a supported R2Conditional), supply the checksum in accepted hex/buffer representation, and handle null on failed precondition. Report explicitly mentions mapping checksum/precondition failures and knows null semantics; do not score this shorthand as a concrete API error.

repair_assessment.quote: Add and enforce short `exp`, `iss`, and `aud` claims
repair_assessment.assessment: Reasonable optional security policy, but short expiry creates renewal behavior absent from current product. It does not replace KV authorization and is not needed to establish the checksum defect.

Pinned source: a4385c092afda23c590189e18dfd557d3c86e363. This supplements the non-exhaustive pre-generation notes without changing them or the raw tree. No target execution, incident, or deployed account is involved.

src/db.js:26-35 defines expiredItemTemplate with a non-null value and an empty metadata.passwd. DB_GetWithMetadata at :135-138 deletes the expired D1 row but returns this template instead of null. src/common.js parsePath yields an empty password when the URL has no password suffix. src/handlers/handleWrite.js:132-143 checks non-null value, compares that empty URL password with the template's empty password, and then calls createPaste. A correctly formed multipart PUT with content, no administration suffix, and an expired row that has not already been removed can therefore reach DB_Put, recreate the row, and receive a new administration capability. createPaste at :18 generates a new password if its supplied password is empty.

This is distinct from intended mutation by an existing valid capability holder. It is also distinct from a global temporary writable state: GET-first merely consumes/deletes the expired row and returns a placeholder; DELETE-first does not recreate it. A later PUT then sees no row. The recreation path requires PUT itself to obtain the expired template.

The conditional impact can be stronger when BASIC_AUTH is configured. src/handlers/handleWrite.js:59-65 intentionally checks global BASIC_AUTH for POST only because normal PUT relies on the per-paste secret. The expired-template password match supplies neither a real original capability nor BASIC_AUTH, yet can create new content. This is a source-proven incorrect authorization/expiry transition, although an actual deployed exploit, critical impact, exposure frequency, and disclosure of original content are not demonstrated.

Returning null immediately after deleting expired rows is a minimal remedy. Verification should independently seed expired fixtures for each first method, with a dedicated passwordless PUT case and BASIC_AUTH configured. Assert no row recreation, no newly issued capability, and consistent not-found responses. Running GET first against the same fixture before PUT would mask the mutation defect by removing the row.
